definition: tiktoken is OpenAI’s fast BPE tokenizer for counting and splitting text the way OpenAI models do.

explainer.lead: How to install tiktoken, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import tiktoken

enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("o200k_base")
tokens = enc.encode("How many tokens is this sentence?")
print(len(tokens), enc.decode(tokens[:3]))

explainer.inAi: Count tokens before calling an API to estimate cost, split documents to fit a context window, or trim chat history.

tiers.eli5: It is a tool that chops text into the same little pieces the model was trained on, so you can count them the way the model does.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to count tokens before sending requests and to split text into model-compatible pieces. A pitfall is using a tokenizer that does not match the target model, which yields wrong counts and mismatched inputs.
tiers.paperLevel: A byte-pair-encoding (BPE) tokenizer, open-sourced by OpenAI in 2022, for counting and splitting text as OpenAI models do. Its limits are those of BPE tokenization and of the specific model's vocabulary it encodes.

explainer.example: Before sending a prompt to an OpenAI model, an engineer runs it through tiktoken to check that the token count fits within the context limit.
